overview: Maenporth is a sheltered, east-facing cove about two miles south-west of Falmouth, with views across Falmouth Bay to Pendennis Castle and over to the St Anthony Head lighthouse. The beach shelves gently, so at low tide there’s a stretch of shallow water that’s good for paddling and swimming.
With a car park, café and toilets right by the sand, it’s an easy, relaxed beach, and a nice change from the busier town beaches in Falmouth.

expect.title: Gentle shallows
expect.text: A gently sloping beach with calm, shallow water at low tide.

expect.title: Watersports
expect.text: There are facilities for launching boats, and it’s used for kayaking and scuba diving.

expect.title: Wildlife
expect.text: The wetland behind the cove attracts birds such as grey herons and little egrets.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: Car park, café and public toilets.

goodToKnow.label: Coast path
goodToKnow.text: The South West Coast Path runs through the cove, so you can walk to Falmouth or towards the Helford.

week.text: A calm-water beach that suits younger children, and sheltered when the wind’s from the west. Pair it with the gardens of the Helford, like Glendurgan, just to the south.

pairWith.why: a valley garden with a maze

tips: Go at low tide for the shallow water.
